observation.visible_scene: A low-angle, looking-up view of an overcast white sky framed by bare deciduous trunks (including a prominent leaning birch-like trunk right of center) and snow-dusted evergreen branches at the edges. Dominating the center is a tall, vertical plume of dark clumped debris—irregular black/brown chunks and a brownish smoky haze at the top—suspended in the air throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The dark debris plume is already present in the first frame and persists to the last; over the excerpt its clumps and the upper brown haze gradually spread outward, so the left and right margins of the cloud become more diffuse and scattered chunks drift apart (expansion/dispersion rather than a single translation).
The internal layout of the floating dark chunks changes continuously frame-to-frame (turbulent, slow drift), with some chunks moving relative to the tree trunks behind them.

The camera slowly pans/tilts: the bare trunk on the right moves progressively toward the right edge of the frame and the right-side evergreen foliage shifts accordingly, while the sky background repositions—this is camera motion, not the trees themselves moving.
No new object enters or leaves; the scene composition (trees, sky, plume) is maintained, only evolving in spread and framing.
outside_clip_unknowns: What produced the plume and whether the ejection began before the first cropped frame.
Whether the debris eventually settles or the plume continues to rise after the last frame.
The ground, source location, and any objects below the bottom edge of the frame.
uncertain_details: The exact material identity of the dark clumps (soil, mulch, or other debris) cannot be confirmed.
It is hard to separate the apparent upward/outward drift of individual chunks from the simultaneous camera tilt.
The precise axis and direction of the camera rotation are inferred only from the steady rightward shift of the right-hand trunk.

NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
